# Prototype screens

One page per route template. 27 screens plus the catch-all, enumerated in the
[screen and flow inventory](/design/screen-flow-inventory). All 28 are written.

Grouped by the flow each one leads with. A screen in several flows appears once,
under its primary, with the full list on its own page.

## F1 Launch and authentication

| Route | What you do here |
|-------|------------------|
| [`/splash`](/prototype/screens/splash) | Nothing. It dwells, then forks to today's prompt or your resume step |
| [`/`](/prototype/screens/root-today) | See today's prompt and start drawing. Also the bouncer for signed-out people |
| [`/sign-up`](/prototype/screens/sign-up) | Sign up, log in, or pick an existing user |

| [`/onboarding/welcome`](/prototype/screens/onboarding-welcome) | Read what Scribl is |

| [`/onboarding/canvas`](/prototype/screens/onboarding-canvas) | Draw. The only step that produces state |
| [`/onboarding/story-select`](/prototype/screens/onboarding-story-select) | Choose to type or record. The branches do not rejoin |
| [`/onboarding/story`](/prototype/screens/onboarding-story) | Write the caption. Typed path only |
| [`/onboarding/walls`](/prototype/screens/onboarding-walls) | Pick the walls, and post. The submit fires here |
| [`/onboarding/ready`](/prototype/screens/onboarding-ready) | Confirm and hand over to the app |

## What a screen page carries

`/onboarding/canvas` is the reference. Every screen page has these sections, in
this order, plus a named extra section where a screen warrants one:

1. **At a glance** -- route, router file, flows, whether it makes any data call.
   A reader deciding whether this screen matters to them should not have to read
   further.
2. **The capture** -- the tile, with the capture commit named, and a plain
   statement of anything it fails to show.
3. **Features** -- one row per thing a person can do, each cited `path:line`
   into the app repo. Capabilities, not a description of the UI, because that is
   what a backlog item gets cut from.
4. **Data calls** -- client method, and the backing handler. Where a screen makes
   no call and instead reads or writes a local store, that is stated outright
   with the store write cited. Silence would read as "we did not check."
5. **State in, state out** -- what it reads on entry, what it leaves behind.
6. **Components** -- what it composes, so a change to a shared component can be
   traced to every screen it lands on.
7. **Notes for planning** -- judgement calls, marked as authored here.

## The data-call convention

Frontend calls go through one typed client, `httpDataClient` in
`src/data/http.ts`, and each method is backed one-to-one by a handler under
`backend/lambda/handlers/`. So a screen's data surface is fully described by the
client methods it reaches, directly or through a store.

Several screens make no call of their own. `/onboarding/canvas` and `/draw`
produce state into a local draft store and hand it onward; `/compose` needs
state from a wall's multi-select; `/splash` reads only local storage. On those
pages the "no direct call" line is a finding, not a gap in the write-up.

The API contract these handlers are being formalised against is still a draft on
an unmerged branch (`engineering-schema-api-contract`, PR #58), so it has no page
on this site yet and is not linked from here. Screen pages describe what the code
does today and treat that contract as proposed, not ratified.
